correctness.rationale: For arbitrary measurable a,b:S^2 -> {±1}, the classical bias is B=-∬sgn(x·y)a(x)b(y), optimized in b to ∫|h_a(y)|. Independently verified the oddness h_a(-y)=-h_a(y), and spherical-lune measure gives sharp geodesic Lipschitz 2/π. For any odd L-Lipschitz function, antipodal superlevel sets A_t and -A_t are 2t/L-separated. Lévy isoperimetry for cap metric neighborhoods implies σ(|h|>t)≤1−sin(t/L) for 0≤t≤Lπ/2; integration gives ∫|h|≤L(π/2−1). At L=2/π this yields maximum bias 1−2/π, reached exactly by opposite hemispherical responses. Therefore P_cl=1−1/π; uniform dot product and singlet correlation give P_singlet=3/4 and positive gap 1/π−1/4. No assumption of antipodal response functions was used. Sympy verified exact integral and gap, separate from source verifier Monte Carlo. This proves classical optimality but not globally optimal quantum value.
